name: GlzToolbar
semanticRole: Arrange navigation, primary actions, contextual actions, and overflow controls in a stable priority-aware command surface.

material.rule: Attached toolbars are usually solid or raised; genuinely floating toolbars may use Thin or Regular Glaze. Control density is compact 32–36px, standard about 40px, and touch about 48px while effective targets retain accessibility floors.

input.keyboard: All toolbar controls are reachable in a predictable order; arrow-key roving focus may be used when appropriate; overflow and command-palette equivalents remain keyboard accessible.
input.focus: Focus clearly identifies the active toolbar control and does not disappear when context changes.
input.hover: Hover may reveal tooltips or secondary actions but no essential command depends on hover.
input.press: Press feedback begins immediately and the toolbar does not reflow during activation.
input.selection: Toggle-like toolbar controls expose selected or pressed state with non-color cues; ordinary actions do not pretend to be selected.

accessibility.role: Use toolbar semantics when controls form one command group; nested control roles remain native.
accessibility.name: Multiple or context-specific toolbars have stable programmatic labels and icon-only actions have accessible action names.
accessibility.state: Disabled, selected or pressed, loading, error, and expanded overflow state are exposed when applicable.
accessibility.value: Value-bearing nested controls retain their native values; ordinary toolbar actions do not invent values.
accessibility.keyboard: All commands, groups, overflow actions, and toggle states are fully keyboard accessible.
accessibility.focus: Focus remains visible and predictable across contextual transformations and overflow open/close cycles.
accessibility.errorAssociation: Command failures are announced through an associated status/error region without replacing the actionable label.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Contextual toolbar morph becomes a direct state change or short crossfade.
accessibility.reducedTransparency: Floating Glaze resolves to opaque Raised material.
accessibility.increasedContrast: Strengthen toolbar boundary, focus, selected controls, and separators only where needed.
accessibility.forcedColors: Use system toolbar/button/focus colors and preserve selected state structurally.
accessibility.largeText: Priority overflow occurs before labels or targets become unusable; essential actions remain discoverable.

fallbacks.reducedMotion: Use direct contextual state changes or short crossfades.
fallbacks.highContrast: Strengthen focus, selected states, and necessary grouping boundaries.
fallbacks.forcedColors: Use platform colors and structural selection/focus cues.
fallbacks.performance: Remove blur and decorative shadow before changing action priority, overflow, or target geometry.

content.overflow: Actions follow priority tiers: P1 visible, P2 visible as space permits, P3 overflow, P4 command palette. Lower-priority actions move to overflow before essential controls compress below usable targets.
content.localization: Action labels and tooltips tolerate expansion; icon-only compression requires complete accessible names and discoverable descriptions where ambiguous.
content.rtl: Action groups, navigation direction, overflow placement, and directional icons mirror semantically.

criteria: One dominant primary action remains visually clear without making every command equally loud.
Priority-driven overflow preserves P1 commands and does not hide essential state.
Contextual toolbar transformations preserve spatial continuity where practical.
Floating Glaze is exceptional; dense attached toolbars remain readable and restrained.
